key_insight: iGC combines a learned somatic hypermutation prior with reinforcement learning to optimize antibody binding while preserving biologically plausible mutation patterns.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a strategy for antibody candidate generation that balances predicted binding improvement, mutation realism, and sequence diversity.
method: Learn a mutation prior from parent–child B-cell lineage pairs, then adapt it to a target affinity-maturation dataset.
Initialize an RL policy from the prior and optimize antigen binding with KL regularization toward the frozen prior.
Use RewardNet and TaxNet in a meta-gradient objective to smooth affinity rewards and penalize reward exploitation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports more than twice the strongest baseline's mutation-site prediction performance, retained SHM sequence structure after RL, and competitive reward–diversity products across candidate-selection cutoffs.
watch_item: The abstract does not report experimental binding validation, so predicted affinity gains require laboratory confirmation.
paper_title: iGC: Antibody Optimization via Reinforcement Learning over a Learned Somatic Hypermutation Prior
